contracts: The request is bound to the intended subject identity; promotion and evaluation-set admission both terminate as rejected, with no baseline or evaluation-set authority mutation and a machine-verifiable non-authorizing result.

The dedicated assertion tests must cover the observable intent of ["py", "-3", ".agents/skills/quick-dev-tdd-adapter/tools/governance_policy.py", "--help"] using bounded fixtures, explicit arguments and expected exit/verdict assertions. Help output, a schema document alone, or an unstarted validator cannot prove the bound acceptance. Do not invoke live backends or mutate the real repository in a negative fixture.

Each declared assertion needs a cer_assertion mapping and a meaningful independent oracle. Tests must invoke the real production entry. The plan is not a behavior observation. Keep governance/constraint failures non-authorizing; do not emit expected-red for them. Preserve all bound Given/When/Then and forbidden outcomes. No placeholder pass or synthetic RED.

An evaluation-set admission request succeeds or marks a seed, package, or Skill version as an evaluation-set authority within TC-D1.
The validator evaluates a different subject than the requested seed, package, or Skill version, or cannot bind the request to its canonical repository-relative identity.
